newsitem.title: USA: Two Calif. children, left by mother, die from heat.
newsitem.headline: Two Calif. children, left by mother, die from heat.

text.p: Two young children died of dehydration after being left alone for several days in a hot, stifling apartment while their mother was believed to have been using drugs, police said Tuesday.

Police in Fresno, 150 miles southeast of San Francisco, submitted their report on the case Tuesday to the local district attorney with a request that two counts of murder be filed against the mother, 29-year-old Debbie Lowe, police Lt. Jerry Davis said.

Lowe's daughters, aged 8 months and 20 months, were found dead when police entered her apartment in Fresno Sunday evening. The 8-month-old baby was found in a crib and her sister under a bed in another room, Davis said.

Police were initially called to another part of town where Lowe, who was acting irrationally and appeared to be under the influence of drugs, told officers her children had been kidnapped, Davis said.
Investigators believe Lowe left her apartment as early as the previous Wednesday. Police found the door locked, the windows closed and the air conditioner turned off, Davis said.

Police suspect that Lowe, who was on parole after a drug conviction, "possibly had been using illegal drugs during the several days her children were in the apartment," Davis said. He did not specify the type of drug.
Those days were the hottest so far this summer in Fresno, with temperatures reaching 107 degrees, Davis said.
Investigators believe the children had been dead for a day or two when they were found. The coroner concluded that they died of high body temperatures resulting in dehydration, Davis said.
A few days before the incident, the father of the youngest child had moved out of the apartment after a domestic dispute, Davis said.

Lowe was arrested Sunday evening on suspicion of murder and parole violation and was being held at the Fresno County jail. Police completed their investigation of the case Tuesday and turned it over to the Fresno County District Attorney's office to decide on charges, Davis said.
